title: Complete summary – MSK pathology: infection, osteonecrosis, arthritis & tumours
html:
Built by reverse-engineering every MCQ of this lecture. 🔁 = asked in several sessions · ⚠ = classic trap.

Osteomyelitis 🔁🔁🔁

  • Staphylococcus aureus, haematogenous spread; starts in the METAPHYSIS (children) – not diaphysis, not facial sinuses ⚠
  • Radiographs normal for 10–14 days; MRI = best early imaging.
  • Chronic: sequestrum, involucrum, cloaca / fistula, sclerosis & cortical thickening. No Codman triangle.
  • Sequestrum (hallmark, "typical for osteomyelitis"): central dense bone (dead bone opacity) + peripheral lucent ring + peripheral osteosclerosis ± fistulous tract. The centre is dense, NOT transparent.
  • Best method to show a sequestrum: CT.
  • "Septic osteonecrosis" common features: sequestration, best shown by CT.

Septic arthritis

  • MRI positive within 24 h; early radiographs normal; later rapid joint-space narrowing; may end in ankylosis. Osteophytes are not typical.

Aseptic osteonecrosis 🔁

  • Location: epiphyses / short bones (femoral head) – not metaphysis.
  • Early diagnosis = MRI; crescent sign = subchondral fracture; cartilage and joint space preserved/enlarged early; NO periosteal reaction.
  • Risk factors: steroids, alcohol.

Joint diseases – the key comparison 🔁🔁🔁

Osteoarthritis (arthrosis)Rheumatoid arthritisAnkylosing spondylitisGout
HallmarkOsteophytesMarginal erosions, periarticular osteopenia ("phalangeal band osteoporosis")Syndesmophytes, bamboo spinePunched-out erosions with overhanging edges, 1st MTP, tophi, normal density
Joint spaceasymmetric narrowinguniform narrowingsacroiliac fusionpreserved late
Othersubchondral sclerosis, cystssymmetric MCP/PIP/wrist; ankylosis only late (stage IV)see belowdistal
  • Osteophytes = degenerative; arise from the vertebral surface/margin, perpendicular (horizontal); correspond to calcified tendon/ligament insertions in degenerative disease. Syndesmophytes = AS; arise at the vertebral angle, run parallel (vertical) ⚠
  • RA: NOT distal interphalangeal joints, NOT pencil-in-cup (= psoriatic), NOT early ankylosis, no large osteophytes.
  • Bone ankylosis may occur in: ankylosing spondylitis, rheumatoid arthritis, septic arthritis – NOT spondylarthrosis, NOT osteomyelitis.

Ankylosing spondylitis (≥ 3 MCQs in 2025!) 🔁🔁🔁

  • Men > women (≈ 2.5–5 : 1). Rule: "close to the midline, away from the distal extremities" (axial skeleton + large proximal joints).
  • Bilateral symmetric sacroiliitis (lower synovial 2/3).
  • Romanus lesions (erosion of anterior vertebral corners) → shiny corners → loss of anterior concavity = square vertebra.
  • Syndesmophytes → bamboo spine; ossified interspinous/supraspinous ligament; "tram-rail" spine (linear opacities along the spine), dagger sign.
  • FALSE statements asked: "ankylosis does not occur" ✗ (it does); "disease located only in SI joints and spine" ✗ (also hips, shoulders, entheses).

Bone tumours 🔁🔁

TumourKey facts
Osteosarcoma10–25 y, metaphysis around the knee, mixed lytic-sclerotic, sunburst, Codman triangle
Ewing sarcomachild/adolescent, DIAPHYSIS, permeative, poorly delineated, multilamellar "onion bulb" (± spiculated) periostosis, large soft-tissue mass; NOT unilamellar, NOT popcorn calcification
Osteochondroma (exostosis)metaphysis of long bones, cortex + medulla continuous with host bone, cartilage cap (MRI), grows away from the joint; malignant change → chondrosarcoma (not osteosarcoma) ⚠
Giant cell tumour20–40 y after physeal closure, eccentric, expansile, osteolytic, epiphyso-metaphyseal reaching subchondral bone, septa ("soap bubble"), NO sclerotic rim, usually no periosteal reaction
Bone haemangiomaVERTEBRAL BODY (asked in 2022, old exam, 2025), vertical striations, bright T1 & T2
Osteomafacial (paranasal) sinuses – frontal > ethmoid; ivory dense; multiple → Gardner
Multiple myelomamultiple punched-out lytic lesions, skull "raindrop", diffuse osteopenia, bone scan often negative
  • Malignant potential: osteochondroma, enchondroma (→ chondrosarcoma), giant cell tumour. Benign without: haemangioma, osteoid osteoma.
